segmentName: Home textile & furnishing retail (India — bedding, curtains, table/kitchen linen)

market.domesticSlice: India-specific figures (Facts & Factors); used as the primary market-size source here in preference to a second source (Custom Market Insights) whose 'bedsheet' sub-category figure was larger than its own 'whole home textile' figure — an internal inconsistency not resolved, so not used.

structureFacts: India's home-textile market is large and growing steadily (~8.4-8.6% CAGR across sources), roughly doubling in size over the coming decade.

The category spans two very different competitor tiers: large, listed, export-scale manufacturers (Welspun India, Indo Count Industries, Trident, Bombay Dyeing, Himatsingka Seide, GHCL, Arvind's home-textiles division) and branded, retail-facing D2C/omnichannel players closer to Swayam's own positioning (Portico New York, Spaces, D'Decor, Sarita Handa, Fabindia, Maspar).

COVID-19 (2020-2021) created a temporary, government-licensed PPE/mask manufacturing opportunity for textile companies broadly — a real, documented industry-wide pivot (many home-textile and garment makers, including Swayam, became certified PPE suppliers) that has since wound down as demand normalized.

adoptionStructure.note: A discretionary, repeat-purchase retail category (bedding/curtains/linens), sold through owned retail counters, multi-brand retail-chain concessions (Shopper's Stop, Pantaloons, @Home, etc.), and online — not a subscription or tender-driven market.

drivers: Design/aesthetic appeal and print variety — a discretionary, style-driven purchase.
Availability across recognized multi-brand retail chains (Shopper's Stop, Pantaloons, @Home, EVOK, Hometown, Spencer's, Hypercity) — trust transfers partly from the retail channel itself.
Basic quality/safety assurance (colorfastness, skin-safety) rather than international eco-certification, for the domestically-focused segment of this market.
customerValue.strongestPredictor: Retail distribution breadth (counters × cities × recognized retail-chain presence) — in a discretionary, browse-and-buy category, being physically present where the shopper already is matters as much as the product itself.
